title: Use a violin only for experts, with its box plot drawn inside it.
rule: Use a violin, a reference form, where a technical audience compares the shapes of several distributions. Draw each group’s smoothed density as a shape mirrored about its center line, with the quartiles and median inside it, and say how the shape was smoothed. Oath & Action draws one only in a methods note or a report for specialists.
use_when: A specialist asks whether a group’s values bunch in one place or two, and the quartiles alone would hide a second hump.

use_instead.when: A general reader compares the spread of a few groups
One group’s shape, with counts a reader can check

text: A violin shows a second hump that a box plot hides, but its width comes from a smoothing choice the reader cannot see. Keeping the box inside it gives every reader the quartiles they can trust.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw a violin only in a specialist piece, from a density the analyst states, with the quartile box inside it as box-plot draws one.
sketch_alt: Three violins, each a mirrored density shape with its quartile box and median inside, side by side on one scale; the middle group has two humps that a box plot alone would hide.
